field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PoC, crafted query string, or regression test was executed; the finding is static. No HTTP request was sent against a Laravel application.

Reachability requires register_argc_argv=On and a non-CLI SAPI that exposes the query string through $_SERVER['argv']. This dossier did not test a specific web server/PHP build combination; the advisory and Debian DLA state the condition but do not enumerate every SAPI.
The fix commit adds no automated regression test; only Application.php changed. Test coverage for the fixed behavior is not evidenced.

The GHSA/OSV record carries a CVSS_V3 vector with all impact metrics N (numeric 0.0) while the same record labels the issue HIGH; NVD's own primary CVSS 3.1 is 7.5 and the CNA CVSS 4.0 is 8.7. The canonical severity uses the NVD primary 7.5 and records the inconsistency rather than propagating the zero vector.

All six per-branch fix commits were verified locally against the named fixed tag and the immediately preceding tag. The 6.x fix is bundled into the v6.20.45 tag commit itself (841d842) and the 7.x fix into a version commit (639b222), so their commit messages do not describe the security change; their diffs still only touch Application.php.

The independent review described the 6.x fix parent as v6.20.44 (505ebcd); local ancestry shows the actual parent is 7e82e1a, a changelog commit created after v6.20.44. The verdict is unaffected because both 7e82e1a and v6.20.44 still contain the unconditional argv read, but the reviewer's parent hash is not reproduced and is recorded here rather than silently corrected in the review artifact.
Debian 11 backported the fix into 6.20.14+dfsg-2+deb11u2, whose version number is below upstream 6.20.45; the Debian package version is not interchangeable with the upstream release boundary.

The vulnerable snapshot is v11.30.0 (11.x). The other five branch ranges are recorded from the advisory families but were not snapshotted; this dossier does not claim a source-level vulnerable snapshot for them.

The concrete security consequence depends on which environment-specific configuration and services are present (for example a .env.<name> file or environment-conditional providers). No exploit chain beyond the environment override was demonstrated.

critical_operation.description: Application::detectEnvironment() forwards $_SERVER['argv'] to EnvironmentDetector without checking the SAPI. EnvironmentDetector::detect() treats any non-empty argv array as console input and getEnvironmentArgument() extracts a value from '--env' or '--env=...'. On a web SAPI with register_argc_argv enabled, PHP populates argv from the query string, so a crafted request such as ?--env=<name> can override app.env. The v11.31.0 fix only forwards argv when runningInConsole() is true.

entry_point.description: LoadConfiguration::bootstrap() calls detectEnvironment() on every application boot, and LoadConfiguration is in the HTTP kernel's bootstrapper list. The externally controlled input is the request query string, which PHP exposes as $_SERVER['argv'] when register_argc_argv is on. The entry point recorded here is the framework call site; the HTTP server and PHP INI setting are environmental preconditions.

open_questions: Which common PHP SAPI/INI combinations expose the raw query string through $_SERVER['argv'] was not surveyed; only the advisory's register_argc_argv=On condition is recorded.
Whether a specific environment name yields a concrete security bypass (debug disclosure, different database, different providers) was not demonstrated.
The 6.x-10.x backport commits were not identified by SHA; only the fixed release contents were checked.

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA (GitHub_M), NVD, FriendsOfPHP, GHSA and Debian all agree on the same six branch boundaries and on the register_argc_argv mechanism. Severity is inconsistent: GHSA's CVSS_V3 vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:N implies 0.0, yet its database_specific severity is HIGH; NVD's own primary CVSS 3.1 is 7.5, and the CNA's CVSS 4.0 is 8.7. The canonical severity uses NVD's primary 7.5 and the zero-impact vector is retained here as a source defect. Debian 11 fixes the same CVE by backporting to 6.20.14+dfsg-2+deb11u2, a lower version string than upstream 6.20.45; that backport is recorded separately and is not folded into the upstream range. Branch packaging differs: the 6.x fix is bundled into the v6.20.45 tag commit (841d842), the 7.x fix into a version commit (639b222), while 8.x-11.x have dedicated commits whose messages name the console check.
